blocks.text: HOPPER&FUCHS , a dynamic Belgian publishing house of art and photography books, is certainly present during the festivities in Paris concerning Photography. Main hotspots are the Grand Palais for Paris Photo fair, Polycopies and a ppr oc he .
The salon a ppr oc he & Polycopies: Julie Calbert – Ēkhō
Julie Calbert’s artist’s book Ēkhō will be presented at a ppr oc he (by the gallery L’ENFANT SAUVAGE) as well as on Polycopies with Andrea Copetti’s TIPI BOOKSHOP, in presence of the artist.
ē k h ō : Something that reproduces or recalls something else; a trace, a mark..

Ēkhō brings together a selection of photographs taken between 2022 and 2026, focusing on the landscape and what remains of the places visited. Fragments, a colour, a detail or a remnant reappear throughout the images and gradually transform. Ēkhō, meaning ‘to echo’ in Ancient Greek, evokes this persistence: an image returns, transformed, and continues to resonate.

There is a moment when the landscape extends beyond the place itself. A form glimpsed lingers in our gaze, then resurfaces, transformed by memory. Ēkhō’s images emerge from this point where recognition begins to falter. A rock becomes an expanse, a mountain emerges within a field of color, a relief turns into skin. This persistence permeates Ēkhō. While the photographs bear witness to places and objects encountered, they gradually emancipate themselves from them. The scales range from the horizon to the infinitesimal, from the distant to the very near. At the center of the book, the Araucaria embodies this state of metamorphosis: a single image unfolds into infinite variations. Its motif becomes embedded in memory while retaining the traces of its successive transformations. Ēkhō means “to return a sound” in Ancient Greek. Here, the image continually returns, at once identical and altered, singular and duplicated. Within this vibrant gap, between matrix and multiple, photography imprints itself on our memories.
Julie Calbert
Paris Photo – Gallery FIFTY ONE: Stig De Block – EAST LOS & dedications by Harry Gruyaert…
Thursday 12 November, 2pm, Book launch and presentation EAST LOS by Stig De Block, Paris Photo, Booth B13

East Los is made in close collaboration with renowned author and former Los Angeles Poet Laureate Luis J. Rodriguez, whose generous gift of his poem “The Eastside Of All Eastsides” became the foundation for my journey through the East of Los Angeles. Inspired by his words, I took long and short walks, had in-depth and short talks.
“ IN EAST LA THE SURFACE NEVER SETTLES” by STIG DE BLOCK

It is scraped, layered, reclaimed, and repainted before it’s painted again. A single wall holds three generations of decisions. Each coat of colour marks a new claim to space, a new attempt to define belonging. East LA is a place where expression and survival merge without permission. Time, in this body of work, is both subject and material. East LA appears not as a fixed geography but as a manuscript of accumulated surfaces. I trace these material histories through façades that recall a real life collage: pastel warehouse walls fading into half-tone cemented windows, wooden reinforcements aligning with neighbouring roofs, and colour fields that evoke the monumental abstraction of a Rothko, though in concrete and plaster.
DEDICATIONS by Harry Gruyaert, Bruno V. Roels and Katrien De Blauwer

The collaboration between Gallery FIFTY ONE and Bruno Devos, creator of art books and publisher at HOPPER&FUCHS, started more than ten years ago. In this period the gallery published some 24 FIFTY ONE publications, sized A5, within a softcover and always looking for the unexpected encounter with photography and drawing by the artists of the gallery. All over the world these publications, introduced and curated by gallery owner Roger Szmulewicz, are like chocolate candy bars, captivating but with lingering aftertastes. At Paris Photo Harry Gruyaert, Bruno V. Roels and Katrien De Blauwer will sign their publications during the fair. Look out at the gallery schedule for book signings.
